name: Apple Notes
description: Apple Notes is Apple's personal notes app for text, checklists, tables, links, scans, attachments, tags, folders, locked notes, and shared iCloud notes.
agentUseSummary: Apple Notes cannot be connected through Relay because Apple publishes user-operated Notes apps and iCloud.com workflows, plus manual file import and per-note export, but no supported third-party API or framework for enumerating or managing a person's Notes library. Relay will not scrape iCloud.com, inspect private Notes databases, drive the Notes app, or collect Apple credentials.

blocked.label: Connect Apple Notes
blocked.description: No connection is exposed because Apple publishes no supported third-party Notes library API, authorization scope, or developer enrollment contract.

blocked.label: Collect Apple credentials
blocked.description: Apple Account passwords, verification codes, cookies, session tokens, app-specific passwords, and private framework material are never collected.

blocked.label: Read notes
blocked.description: Notes, folders, tags, attachments, scans, locked content, collaborators, and account metadata remain unavailable.

blocked.label: Change notes or use private interfaces
blocked.description: Creating, editing, deleting, moving, sharing, or unlocking notes, scraping iCloud.com, reading private databases, AppleScript or UI automation, arbitrary endpoints, and raw responses are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No Apple Notes action or credential path is exposed.

providerSetup.blocker: Apple documents Notes as an Apple-device and iCloud.com application. Its supported interchange is user-operated file import and per-note PDF or Markdown export; current developer documentation does not publish a Notes data framework, delegated authorization scope, server endpoint contract, webhook, or enrollment path for a third party to enumerate or manage a user's Notes library.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep Apple Notes unavailable unless Apple publishes a supported third-party Notes API with least-authority delegated authorization. Do not substitute iCloud.com scraping, private database access, AppleScript, device automation, or Apple Account credentials; user-selected exported files belong in a separate explicit file-import workflow.

evidence.supports: Apple documents viewing, creating, editing, organizing, deleting, searching, and sharing iCloud notes through the signed-in iCloud.com user interface, not through a third-party developer API.
Apple documents user-operated import of text, Markdown, HTML, RTF, RTFD, and ENEX files and per-note PDF or Markdown export in the Mac Notes app; it does not present this as an account API.
Apple documents Notes synchronization by signing the same Apple Account into Apple devices and using the Notes app or iCloud.com.
Apple's developer guidance limits app data sharing to an app's own iCloud containers and app groups, rather than granting access to another app's private Notes data.
